Re: CRU2024001 Review of Large Energy Users connection policy 
Introduction 
1. The Irish Planning Institute (IPI) welcomes the opportunity to provide our views on the 
consultation paper on the review of Large Energy Users (LEU) connection policy. In 
particular the Institute wishes to comment regarding the approach to the location of LEUs. 
 
2. Founded in 1975, the Irish Planning Institute is the all-island professional body representing 
professional planners engaged in physical, spatial and environmental planning in Ireland and 
Irish planners practicing overseas. Representing over 1,000 planners across the public and 
private sector, members of the Irish Planning Institute work in Local Authorities, An Bord 
Pleanála, Central Government, Regional Assemblies, Academia, in Private Practice as 
Consultants, for large developers and for semi state organisations. 
Alignment with Spatial Planning Policy 
3. The Institute is concerned that the consultation paper has limited integration with spatial 
planning policy and little regard for the potential land use planning implications of future 
LEU connection policy — particularly for those LEUs with significant employment potential 
and thus transport requirements.  
 
4. It is essential that CRU LEU policy links with national, regional and local planning policy — 
especially the National Planning Framework which is currently being revised.  The preferred 
location policy as articulated in the consultation paper fails to identify the spatial 
implications of such an approach. This includes considering the implications for our compact 
growth, regional development, sustainable transport, biodiversity, landscape and 
environmental objectives and obligations, all of which are required to be considered in 
forward planning and development management processes. 
 
5. While there may be merit in locating new LEUs close to renewable generation and storage 
and in less constrained parts of the network, including from a balanced regional 
development perspective, given the varied profile of LEUs, a one size fits all approach is not 
appropriate. Any approach to individual projects must also align with relevant local 
development plan policy under the National Planning Framework.  
District Heating 
6. Regarding the discussion of district heating in the paper, it is unclear how waste heat from 
LEUs can be utilised in district heating if the preference is to locate them in less constrained 
locations, close to renewables, which are likely to be distant from population centres.

2 
 
Conclusion 
7. The forthcoming CRU policy needs to be based on a partnership approach with 
stakeholders, including planning authorities, and must align with our national, local and 
regional planning policies. The Institute appreciates the opportunity to provide its views as 
part of consultation. If the Institute can be of any further assistance, please do not hesitate 
to contact us.  
Is mise le meas, 
 
 
 
Dr Seán O’Leary MIPI 
Senior Planner
